prompt: In Ana's Dockerfile, `RUN go build …` and `CMD ["shelf"]` both run programs. When does each run?
hint: One makes the image; the other is what the image does.

choices.text: Both run every time a container starts, in order
choices.why: Then every start would recompile; the build result is already in a layer.
Right. `RUN`'s result is stored as a layer; `CMD` is the container's default command.
`CMD` is recorded during the build and run later, by each container.
The other way round.

prompt: Ana's Dockerfile says `EXPOSE 8080`. What made `curl localhost:8080` work on her machine?

choices.why: `EXPOSE` documents the port; it publishes nothing.
That sets a directory; it has nothing to do with ports.
Right. Publishing happens at run time.

choices.text: Go opens host ports by default for any program it compiles
choices.why: The program listens inside the container's network namespace.

prompt: In the first build, step `#8`, `go build`, took 14.2 seconds. Why so long for a small service?

choices.text: It downloads pgx from the internet
choices.why: pgx is vendored; nothing was downloaded.
`RUN` runs at normal speed inside the build.
Building does not run tests; that is `go test`.

choices.text: It also compiles the standard library and pgx
choices.why: Right, from scratch, since nothing was cached yet.

prompt: `docker image ls shelf` showed the first image's `DISK USAGE`. How many GB?
With `CMD shelf`, `docker stop` took ten seconds and `shelf` never logged "shutting down". Why?

choices.text: `/bin/sh -c shelf` was process 1 and did not pass `SIGTERM` on
choices.why: Right. Docker waited, then sent `SIGKILL` to both.

choices.text: `shelf` ignores `SIGTERM` when it is started without a JSON list
choices.why: The same binary handled `SIGTERM` in exec form; it never received it here.

choices.text: Docker always waits ten seconds before stopping a container, whatever it runs
choices.why: In exec form it stopped in a fifth of a second.
It had one, and ports have nothing to do with signals.

prompt: If a container really needs a shell script to start, the script should start the program with `___ shelf`, so that the program replaces the shell as process 1.
hint: A shell builtin of four letters.

prompt: After `docker build --build-arg VERSION=1.0.0`, which variable does `docker image inspect` find in the image's `Env`?
hint: One lives during the build; the other in every container.

choices.why: `VERSION` was an `ARG`; it existed only while the build ran.
Right. `ENV` is stored in the image; the version reached the binary through the linker instead.

choices.text: Only `VERSION`, since it was given on the command line
choices.why: Command-line build arguments are not stored as environment.
`ENV` variables are: `PORT=8080` is in the list.

prompt: The image says `ENV PORT=8080`, and Ana runs it with `-e PORT=9090`. Which port does `shelf` listen on?

choices.why: The log says `:9090`; run-time values override the image's.
The program reads one value of `PORT`.
Right: `docker run -e` overrides `ENV`.
There is no conflict; one simply overrides the other.

The directory later instructions and the container start in

prompt: Ana's `.env` ended up in `shelf:dev`. She adds `RUN rm /src/.env` after the `COPY`. Is the password gone from the image?
hint: What does each instruction leave behind?

choices.text: No; the earlier `COPY` layer still has it
choices.why: Right. The fix is keeping it out of the context with `.dockerignore`; lesson 14 shows the layer.

choices.text: Yes, the file no longer exists
choices.why: It no longer appears in the final filesystem, but the layer from `COPY` still holds it.

choices.text: Yes, if she also runs `docker image prune`
choices.why: Pruning removes unused images, not layers of this one.

choices.text: No, because `rm` is not allowed in a Dockerfile
choices.why: `rm` runs fine; it just cannot reach back into an earlier layer.

prompt: After adding `.dockerignore`, the build reported `transferring context: 22.75kB`, less than `vendor/` alone. Why?
hint: What did the builder already have?

choices.why: `ls -a /src` shows `vendor` in the image.

choices.text: BuildKit sent only what changed since earlier builds
choices.why: Right. The number counts the transfer, not the size of the context.

choices.text: BuildKit compresses the context to 0.3% of its size
choices.why: Compression does not explain it; the source is barely compressible.

choices.text: The build failed and sent nothing
choices.why: It named `shelf:dev` and the image has its files.

prompt: An image has `ENTRYPOINT ["yq"]` and `CMD ["--help"]`. What runs for `docker run image ".a" f.yaml`?

choices.why: Arguments after the image name replace `CMD`.
That would happen with no entrypoint.
Right: the entrypoint stays, the typed arguments replace the default ones.
Typed arguments replace `CMD`; they are not appended to it.
